transcript.title: Opening
transcript.text: Good morning Rushil Bhatia. Here is your daily news for Tuesday, September 29. In today's briefing: top headlines, bhopal and madhya pradesh, business and markets, money, tax and personal finance, science and technology, development and policy, across india, around the world. Let's begin.

transcript.title: Top headlines
transcript.text: First, the stories leading the news this morning. Khalistan groups turn to jail networks to recruit operatives across north India: Intel. Intelligence agencies are investigating pro-Khalistan groups recruiting within jails across north India. A recently detained operative disclosed connections to key figures while serving in Patiala jail. Agency investigations now focus on dead-drop recruitment methods and funding channels used by these groups. An SFJ-backed operatives was arrested after graffiti incidents linked to Khalistan activities. Bruce Willis built Parrot Cay compound with 3 homes, sold for $27M in 2019. Bruce Willis has finalized the sale of his expansive 7.3-acre beachfront estate on Parrot Cay for a staggering $27 million. Acquired in 2000, the land saw the addition of three custom built homes over four years, nestled within 12 bedrooms and 14 elegant bathrooms. With luxurious outdoor spaces featuring multiple swimming pools, this sale marks a record-breaking residential deal in the Caribbean, as Willis actively streamlines his property portfolio. How Stephen and Ayesha Curry built an empire while giving back to Oakland. Stephen and Ayesha Curry have built successful careers beyond basketball and Hollywood while maintaining a strong connection to Oakland. Stephen expanded into media through Unanimous Media, while Ayesha grew Sweet July into a lifestyle brand spanning food, skincare and content. Through Eat. Learn. India's Essar Group to invest $18 billion in 'largest' US steel plant, Trump announces. US President Donald Trump on Monday announced plans by Indian conglomerate Essar Group, through its US subsidiary Mesabi Metallics, to invest about $18 billion in a major steel plant in Iowa. Delhi Police file non-cognisable report against Parvesh Verma after complaint over slap. Delhi Police has submitted a non-cognisable report after a complaint involving PWD minister Parvesh Verma. The complaint was filed by Sahib Singh, who reported being slapped by the minister. Additionally, an FIR related to extortion was registered by an assistant engineer of the PWD. AAP national convener Arvind Kejriwal has demanded Verma's dismissal and arrest. 'Can at times evade human oversight': OpenAI scraps release of latest ChatGPT model. OpenAI has delayed the release of its next-generation artificial intelligence model, GPT-6.1 Astra, after the system failed to meet the company's internal safety standards. US military to guard midterms after Trump gutted agency that protects elections. The National Security Agency and other military cyber units have long assisted with monitoring election infrastructure and defending it against possible hacking attempts. Election systems were designated as "critical infrastructure" in 2017, paving the way for greater federal cybersecurity support. Hegseth's announcement comes weeks before Election Day on November 3, with early voting already underway. Scandal-built 1914 Massachusetts mansion listed for $3.5M with ballroom. A stunning Gilded Age estate known as The Crossways has hit the market for a price tag of $3.5 million. This historic home, built in 1914, is deeply connected to Hopedale's Draper family. It showcases exquisite original craftsmanship, alongside modern amenities like central air and hydro-air heating. Nestled on 2.36 acres, it boasts beautifully designed Italian gardens and an inviting outdoor pool, reflecting Hopedale's rich industrial history. 'I offered nothing': Trump denies sanctions relief to Iran, bashes media report. US President Donald Trump on Monday denied offering Iran any concessions, after a report emerged that Washington was willing to provide sanctions relief and release frozen Iranian funds as part of a final agreement if Tehran makes "concrete progress" on the nuclear issue. Bill Gates Foundation to shut down in 2045: Why some Americans reject its $400m 'gift'. The Bill Gates Foundation has committed $1 billion to the advancement of equitable AI technologies across various sectors globally. Of this substantial investment, $400 million is earmarked for educational programs aimed at developing AI-enhanced tutoring systems that tailor learning processes in classrooms. Meanwhile, New York City schools have implemented a moratorium on student-accessible generative AI. The foundation's ambitious plans anticipate completion by 2045. Government to tighten rules to block under-18 accounts on social media platforms. Agreeing with Supreme Court, Centre on Monday said it would soon insert a provision in the Information and Technology Intermediary Rules to prevent social media intermediaries from allowing children under 18 years of age to open social media accounts, reports Dhananjay Mahapatra. Why hotel towels have stripes: The real reason behind the design. Horizontal stripes on hotel towels not only contribute to a sleek and polished appearance but also signify their durability and quality. These stripes facilitate easier folding for housekeeping, ensuring an immaculate presentation in every room. While some believe the stripes enhance hygiene, true cleanliness relies more on meticulous washing practices.
